question: Who is identified in Colossians 1:7 as the faithful minister of Christ who originally taught the Colossians the gospel?
opt1: Epaphras our dear fellowservant, who is for you a faithful minister of Christ
opt2: Tychicus the beloved messenger from the province of Asia
opt3: Aristarchus the Macedonian fellowprisoner from Thessalonica
opt4: Archippus the resident pastor of the congregation at Colosse
correct: Epaphras our dear fellowservant, who is for you a faithful minister of Christ
explanation: Epaphras was the native evangelist who first brought the gospel to Colosse and reported their spiritual progress to Paul. Colossians 1:7 (KJV) - "As ye also learned of Epaphras our dear fellowservant, who is for you a faithful minister of Christ;"

question: For what spiritual fruitfulness and knowledge did Paul cease not to pray for the Colossians in Colossians 1:9-10?
opt1: Endowed with vast commercial wealth through merchant ventures in the Lycus valley
opt2: Filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding; that ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing
opt3: Granted political immunity from Roman provincial taxes and military conscription
opt4: Equipped with ancient Greek rhetoric to debate philosophers in public amphitheaters
correct: Filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding; that ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing
explanation: Paul petitioned God that their theological comprehension of His will would translate into a worthy, pleasing, and fruitful walk. Colossians 1:9-10 (KJV) - "For this cause we also, since the day we heard it, do not cease to pray for you, and to desire that ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding; That ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God;"

question: From what dark domain has the Father delivered believers, and into what realm has He translated them in Colossians 1:13?
opt1: Delivered us from physical poverty and translated us into earthly palaces
opt2: Rescued us from Roman civic courts and translated us to municipal governance
opt3: Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son
opt4: Delivered us from manual craftsmanship and translated us into academic schools
correct: Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son
explanation: Regeneration transfers believers out of the tyrannical dominion of Satan directly into the glorious kingdom of God's beloved Son. Colossians 1:13 (KJV) - "Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son:"

question: What redemptive blessing do believers possess in Christ through His sacrificial blood in Colossians 1:14?
opt1: A written exemption from physical aging and biological disease on earth
opt2: A title deed guaranteeing personal real estate holdings in Palestine
opt3: An imperial certificate granting social prestige among Roman senators
opt4: In whom we have redemption through his blood, even the forgiveness of sins

explanation: Believers possess complete redemption and absolute pardon for all sins purchased exclusively through the blood of Christ. Colossians 1:14 (KJV) - "In whom we have redemption through his blood, even the forgiveness of sins:"

question: How does the apostle Paul describe the divine supremacy and creative agency of Christ in Colossians 1:15-16?
opt1: Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature: for by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth
opt2: Who was an exalted archangel created by the Father prior to the creation of the world
opt3: Who was a human prophet endowed with temporary miraculous power during his ministry
opt4: Who was an allegorical figure representing divine wisdom in Jewish philosophical thought
correct: Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature: for by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth
explanation: Christ is the visible manifestation of the invisible God, holding sovereign preeminence (firstborn) over all creation as its Maker. Colossians 1:15-16 (KJV) - "Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature: For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him:"

question: What cosmic role does Christ maintain over all created things according to Colossians 1:17?
opt1: He watches passively while the material universe operates by blind natural fate
opt2: And he is before all things, and by him all things consist
opt3: He shares sovereign oversight of nature with regional angelic principalities
opt4: He intervened once at creation but withdrew from sustaining the physical order
correct: And he is before all things, and by him all things consist
explanation: Christ possesses eternal pre-existence, continuously holding together and sustaining the entire fabric of the universe (consist). Colossians 1:17 (KJV) - "And he is before all things, and by him all things consist."

question: What position of headship and preeminence does Christ hold in relation to the church in Colossians 1:18?
opt1: He is an honorary patron alongside the senior apostles residing in Jerusalem
opt2: He is the earthly prophet who founded an administrative council in Antioch
opt3: And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence
opt4: He is a spiritual teacher whose instructions are evaluated by church elders
correct: And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence
explanation: As the resurrected Head of the church, Christ possesses absolute, unrivaled preeminence over both creation and the new creation. Colossians 1:18 (KJV) - "And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence."

question: How was universal peace and reconciliation accomplished by God according to Colossians 1:20?
opt1: Through political diplomacy negotiated between Roman governors and the Sanhedrin
opt2: By enforcing the ceremonial ordinances and dietary washings of the Mosaic law
opt3: Through mystical ascetic rituals revealed to the philosophical sages of Phrygia

explanation: Divine reconciliation was achieved through the substitutionary, atoning sacrifice of Christ's cross, making peace for alienated sinners. Colossians 1:20 (KJV) - "And, having made peace through the blood of his cross, by him to reconcile all things unto himself; by him, I say, whether they be things in earth, or things in heaven."

question: What is the glorious mystery hid from ages and generations that is now manifested to the saints in Colossians 1:26-27?
opt1: Which is Christ in you, the hope of glory
opt2: The secret numerical codes embedded in the genealogies of the patriarchs
opt3: The physical restoration of the temple altar upon Mount Moriah in Jerusalem

correct: Which is Christ in you, the hope of glory
explanation: The magnificent mystery of the New Covenant is the indwelling presence of Christ within Gentile believers as the pledge of eternal glory. Colossians 1:27 (KJV) - "To whom God would make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles; which is Christ in you, the hope of glory:"

question: What was the supreme goal of Paul's preaching and ministerial labor in Colossians 1:28?
opt1: To amass large monetary funds from the churches of Phrygia for his retirement
opt2: Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom; that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus
opt3: To convince Roman magistrates to grant Christianity legal status as an official cult
opt4: To establish academic academies in Asia Minor to compete with Greek philosophers
correct: Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom; that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus
explanation: Paul's pastoral mission was to proclaim Christ comprehensively, guiding every believer into spiritual maturity and perfection in Christ. Colossians 1:28 (KJV) - "Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom; that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus:"

question: What divine treasures are declared to be hid in Christ according to Colossians 2:3?
opt1: Vast repositories of gold and silver guarded by angels in heaven

opt4: Esoteric magical incantations to ward off regional demon spirits

explanation: All true spiritual wisdom, divine understanding, and knowledge reside exclusively and exhaustively in the person of Jesus Christ. Colossians 2:3 (KJV) - "In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge."

question: How are believers commanded to walk in Christ Jesus the Lord in Colossians 2:6-7?
opt1: By continually seeking new revelations beyond what the apostles preached

correct: Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught, abounding therein with thanksgiving
explanation: Just as they received Christ by faith, believers must continue growing firmly rooted, established in orthodox truth, and full of gratitude. Colossians 2:7 (KJV) - "Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught, abounding therein with thanksgiving."

question: Against what deceptive human systems does Paul issue an urgent warning in Colossians 2:8?
opt1: Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ

opt3: Beware lest municipal tax collectors demand excessive tariffs on imported goods

correct: Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ
explanation: Paul warns against being spiritually plundered (spoil) by hollow, deceptive philosophies and legalistic human traditions that replace Christ. Colossians 2:8 (KJV) - "Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ."

opt1: Christ holds partial deity which must be supplemented by angelic intercessors
opt2: For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily. And ye are complete in him, which is the head of all principality and power
opt3: Believers must undergo ceremonial initiations to attain spiritual completeness
opt4: The divine nature was divided among the prophets and apostles across history
correct: For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily. And ye are complete in him, which is the head of all principality and power
explanation: The entirety of essential deity resides permanently in Christ's bodily person, and believers find their complete spiritual perfection in Him. Colossians 2:9-10 (KJV) - "For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily. And ye are complete in him, which is the head of all principality and power:"

Colossians 2:14 (KJV) - "Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross;"

question: Why does Paul command believers not to let anyone judge them regarding food, drink, feast days, new moons, or sabbaths in Colossians 2:16-17?
opt1: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ

opt4: Because dietary laws apply only to believers residing in the province of Judea
correct: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ
explanation: Old Testament dietary and calendar rituals were merely transient shadows pointing forward to their ultimate substance (the body) in Christ. Colossians 2:17 (KJV) - "Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ."

opt4: Submitting to civil magistrates and paying imperial taxes
correct: In a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind

Colossians 2:18 (KJV) - "Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind,"

Colossians 2:19 (KJV) - "And not holding the Head, from which all the body by joints and bands having nourishment ministered, and knit together, increaseth with the increase of God."

Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth."

Lie not one to another, seeing that ye have put off the old man with his deeds;"

question: How should believers conduct their speech toward those outside the faith in Colossians 4:6?
